closed_stream_theorem.statement: An output stream has a preimage iff each observed A|B seam has an adjacent observed B|A seam connected through the appropriate singleton word.
closed_stream_theorem.source_swaps_disjoint: A shared position would have to be both B on the right side of one marked seam and A on the left side of another. A!=B forbids this. Adjacent seams can share a nonsingleton word, but not the same position.
closed_stream_theorem.inverse_variables: Every actual source swap leaves a visible B|A at that same seam. Select any subset of observed B|A seams to invert. These inverse swaps also have disjoint positions.
closed_stream_theorem.monotonicity: At a seam not selected for inversion, a neighboring inverse swap can only change its LEFT endpoint A→B through a singleton left word, or its RIGHT endpoint B→A through a singleton right word. Either change destroys A|B rather than creating it.
closed_stream_theorem.clauses: Each observed A|B seam therefore requires at least one linked neighboring B|A variable to be selected. A selected B|A becomes exactly a marked source A|B. All constraints are positive OR clauses.
closed_stream_theorem.canonical_witness: Selecting ALL visible B|A variables satisfies every satisfiable clause. Invert them simultaneously, then forward-encode the entire candidate to recover the original output exactly.
closed_stream_theorem.complexity: Membership and one preimage are linear scans. Enumerating all preimages may still be exponential; no unique inverse or intended source is claimed.

open_run_padding_theorem.important_distinction: Both artificial pad WORDS have length TWO. Only a first or last word of the OBSERVED RUN may be a singleton for an external rescue.
open_run_padding_theorem.left_boundary: The left pad ends in B, so its seam with the run cannot be A|B. It is B|A exactly when the first run word begins in A. Inverting that seam affects the first INTERNAL seam only if the first run word is singleton A.
open_run_padding_theorem.right_boundary: The right pad begins in A, so its seam with the run cannot be A|B. It is B|A exactly when the last run word ends in B. Inverting that seam affects the last INTERNAL seam only if the last run word is singleton B.
open_run_padding_theorem.equivalence: Closed membership of [BB]+run+[AA] is equivalent to every internal A|B seam having an observed singleton-linked B|A neighbor, or the relevant first/last-run singleton rescue. The padding creates no new unsupported A|B requirement.
open_run_padding_theorem.construction: Apply the closed canonical inverse to the PADDED output and verify its complete forward roundtrip. This is an existential local completion; stripping pads afterward does not license treating run boundaries as closed document boundaries.
